title: Expectation, bias and the decision tree
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What are you expecting from them before they speak?
Jose said that we naturally have biases and prejudices, and that expectations can be synonymous with bias. We say: that guy is a jerk, before we have listened.
He said that being present means moment-to-moment awareness of what is happening, without bias and prejudice, rather than getting caught in the story in your head.

Jose said that he builds a decision tree before a meeting: what if he goes this way, what if he says that? He goes through four or five scenarios, like jiu-jitsu, where you can do eighteen moves in ten seconds, so you are not thrown off your game.
He said that a live example of the group's own calls shows a theory working, and that he wants the students to feel live examples and not stay in the theory.
Jose said that when someone does not meet your expectation and you have labeled it, you then go and search for the meaning, and they will know.
He said that our brains are built for speed and not for accuracy, because we are compulsive thinkers in a compulsive society.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write an expectation you have of someone.
Write what else could be true.
Write three scenarios for your next meeting.
Write what you will pay attention to in the moment.

check.q: What did Jose say expectations can be?
How many scenarios did Jose say he goes through?
What did Jose say being present is?

recap: Notice your expectation. Build the tree. Stay present.
